title: Welcome to Weed Island
gist: Jersey, a self-governing Crown Dependency of 100,000 people, has become an outsized medical cannabis exporter led by Northern Leaf, which exported GBP 8.4 million in 2025. The article covers its regulatory advantages, a push to process and package on-island, local backlash and mental-health concerns, and a CBD loophole allowing legal THC sales that the government may close.

insights.claim: Jersey exported over 9,200 kilograms of medical cannabis in 2025, small versus UK growers but large per capita for an island of 45 square miles and 100,000 people.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: A small jurisdiction is carving out an export niche in medical cannabis.

insights.claim: Northern Leaf accounts for 90 percent of Jersey's cannabis production and exported GBP 8.4 million (about $11.3 million) of medical marijuana in 2025 to markets including the UK and Germany; regulations let it grow only for export.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Supplier concentration in one company creates single-name risk for the island's industry.

insights.claim: Northern Leaf was valued at just GBP 3.7 million in 2024 after a failed IPO despite up to GBP 30 million spent on its facility, and CEO Steven Tan has since lifted capacity from 25 to 75 percent.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: A distressed-asset turnaround, where operational ramp is the value driver.

insights.claim: Tan claims that using 20 percent of Jersey's land he could build a cannabis industry worth more than the island's GBP 40 million potato industry, versus roughly a quarter of it on 5 percent of the land now.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: CEO growth ambition is a promotional claim, unproven.

insights.claim: Jersey legalized medical cannabis in 2019, five private clinics operate, and about 6 percent of the population is prescribed cannabis versus an estimated 0.4 percent in Germany and 0.1 percent in the UK.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Very high prescribing rates raise regulatory and reputational scrutiny of the model.

insights.claim: The converted greenhouse that formerly grew Jersey tomatoes was nearly lost to rising fuel costs and cheaper overseas competition, and Tan lobbies for an industrial energy tariff to ease spiraling energy costs.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Energy costs remain a margin threat for greenhouse cultivation.

insights.claim: Jersey growers are inspected by the UK MHRA, giving buyers confidence in quality, while a small local team can issue permits within a day, an advantage barrister Sarah Clover says is hard to replicate.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Fast permitting plus a UK-grade quality stamp is a defensible edge for a small jurisdiction.

insights.claim: Jersey law currently permits only bulk raw cannabis exports for others to process and pack, though Northern Leaf already has facilities to package finished product and awaits a possible law change.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: A rule change would let Jersey capture more of the value chain, with upside for Northern Leaf.

insights.claim: Tan wants to move into genetics and a tissue-culture lab, saying Jersey could host "the Monsanto of cannabis," a reference to Monsanto's $66 billion acquisition by Bayer in 2018.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Signals aspiration toward IP-rich genetics rather than commodity growing.

insights.claim: Sarah Clover says Jersey could become a life sciences hub for cannabis and other pharmaceuticals, but the island is "on this seesaw" over which way policy will go.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Policy direction is the swing factor for sector growth.

insights.claim: Residents have objected to each expansion of Northern Leaf, with complaints of cannabis smell and concerns about misuse despite all product being exported.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Local opposition is a recurring expansion constraint.

insights.claim: Cannabis is a "contributory factor" in 22 percent of admissions to Jersey's acute mental health ward, according to the island's health minister.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Health data could drive tighter prescribing regulation.

insights.claim: A patient said he was prescribed 30 grams a month after a quick assessment and later was told by a psychiatrist he should never have been prescribed it, and police say resale by "user-dealers" undermines the legal framework.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Prescribing laxity and diversion are enforcement and reputational risks for the medical model.

insights.claim: Cannabis-related offenses in Jersey fell from 216 in 2016 to just 12 as of July 2026.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Supporters can cite falling offenses as evidence in favor of reform.

insights.claim: Jersey law caps THC in CBD products at 3 percent of the CBD weight, so shops like Bailiwick Botanicals sell THC edibles by boosting CBD content, which owner Gary Tucker calls "just a math equation."
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: A regulatory loophole created a gray recreational market that may be closed.

insights.claim: Jersey's government says abuse of its limits is a concern and that it is considering whether the CBD exemptions need amending.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: The loophole business faces material regulatory risk.

insights.claim: Customs raided Bailiwick Botanicals in February 2024 and stock was returned only six months later; as of June 2026 it sells THC edibles and coffee beans and police have stayed away.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Enforcement posture has softened, but remains uncertain.

insights.claim: A 2024 vote to decriminalize recreational cannabis failed by a single vote, a later attempt was withdrawn before debate, and it is expected to return to parliament in the coming months, while possession penalties remain up to five years and supply up to 14 years.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: Decriminalization remains a live near-term catalyst.

insights.claim: Full legalization is limited because Jersey is a signatory to the UN drugs convention via the UK, and the UK blocked Bermuda's 2022 recreational legalization by withholding Royal Assent.
insights.speaker: Orlando Crowcroft
insights.so_what: UK veto precedent makes an "Amsterdam on the Sea" outcome unlikely.
